recent_posts.title: How Vanta automates SOC 2 compliance for startups
recent_posts.summary: A promotional pitch for Vanta, a compliance automation platform that helps startups achieve SOC 2 and other security certifications without dedicated compliance teams. Vanta integrates with GitHub, AWS, and Google Workspace, monitors security controls continuously, maps to 35+ frameworks, and claims to cut audit prep time by 82%. It also provides a trust center for prospects to self-serve compliance reports.

recent_posts.title: OpenAI built a Windows sandbox for Codex in Rust while others did nothing
recent_posts.summary: Most AI coding tools on Windows lack proper sandboxing, unlike Linux and macOS which have built-in solutions. OpenAI addressed this gap by building a custom Windows security sandbox from scratch in Rust for their Codex app, using native Windows features like restricted tokens, file system ACLs, dedicated sandbox users, and firewall rules. The project was open-sourced, making it the only AI coding tool to implement proper sandboxing on Windows.

recent_posts.title: Building a miniature Yamaha network from Japanese gachapon toy machines
recent_posts.summary: A fun experience of finding and collecting miniature Yamaha networking equipment (routers, switches, and access points) from gachapon capsule toy machines in Japan, then assembling them into a display 'full network'. The tiny models even include miniature Ethernet cables.

recent_posts.title: Perplexity Computer review from someone who builds their own AI systems
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on personal experience with Perplexity Computer, a $200/month cloud-based AI agent platform with 19 models and Firecracker microVM sandboxes. The author, who built elaborate custom AI infrastructure with Claude Code and multiple agents, was surprised to find Perplexity Computer accomplished similar tasks with zero setup. Key features covered include a meta-router that selects the best model per subtask, isolated compute environments (Firecracker microVMs), shared file workspaces between agents, scheduled/cron jobs, and cloud-persistent execution. The author built a Blockbuster POS simulator, a kids gaming website, and a cult investigation dashboard. Main critique is cost — the credit system burns fast. The deeper reflection is that over-engineering AI tooling can consume all creative energy, leaving none for actually using the tools.

recent_posts.title: Mem Palace gives AI agents persistent memory via MCP
recent_posts.summary: Mem Palace is an open-source AI memory tool co-created by actress Milla Jovovich and a collaborator named Ben. It claims to be the highest-scoring AI memory system ever benchmarked and is free to use with nearly 5,000 GitHub stars. The tool organizes past AI conversations into a hierarchical structure of wings, halls, and rooms to enable permanent, searchable memory for AI agents. It also introduces a custom AI-readable dialect that compresses months of conversations into ~120 tokens. A live walkthrough covers installation via pip, initializing against a local directory (like an Obsidian vault), mining Claude Code conversations, and connecting it to Claude via MCP.

recent_posts.title: Gemma 4 on the iPhone (local AI, no internet required)
recent_posts.summary: Google's Gemma 4 open-source AI models can now run entirely on-device via the AI Edge Gallery app, with no internet connection required. The demo showcases the 2B and 4B parameter models running on an iPhone in airplane mode, handling text queries, image recognition, and audio input at impressive speeds. A separate mobile actions model can even control phone functions like the flashlight via voice commands, highlighting the growing potential of edge AI computing.

recent_posts.title: Anthropic ends support for third-party harnesses like OpenClaw
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic is officially ending full support for third-party AI harnesses, specifically calling out OpenClaw. The author, who uses OpenClaw with Anthropic's Claude models, is frustrated by this decision and worries it will push users away from Claude toward OpenAI. The post speculates about the future viability of third-party harnesses as AI providers tighten their ecosystems.

recent_posts.title: Axios npm supply chain attack explained with remediation steps
recent_posts.summary: The Axios npm package (100M+ weekly downloads) was compromised in a sophisticated supply chain attack. A hacker obtained the lead maintainer's npm access token, then added a malicious dependency (plain-crypto.js) to package.json rather than modifying Axios source code directly. This dependency's postinstall script deployed a remote access Trojan (RAT) in 1.1 seconds, then erased all traces of itself. Two release branches (1.14.1 and 0.30.4) were poisoned within 39 minutes of each other, meaning any project using caret ranges would automatically pull the compromised version. The post walks through how the attack worked, how to check if your system is affected, and remediation steps including rotating all credentials if compromised.

recent_posts.title: Getting started with OpenClaw AI agent gateway on a VPS
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on walkthrough of OpenClaw, an AI agent gateway with 308k GitHub stars. The video covers installing OpenClaw on a VPS via Hostinger, connecting it to OpenAI or Anthropic models, setting up a Telegram bot interface, and exploring the file-based memory system (soul.md, identity, memory files). Practical demos include building a news briefing dashboard and an IT monitoring agent in seconds. Security considerations are addressed including the security audit command, firewall setup, tools profile configuration, red lines, and warnings about malware in the ClawHub skills marketplace. The author shares personal use cases including an AI IT team, a Japanese-speaking personal assistant, and a fitness coach agent.

recent_posts.title: YouTube's recommendation algorithm bug caused a global outage while ads kept running
recent_posts.summary: YouTube experienced a global outage where the homepage went blank, apps showed error screens, and services like YouTube Music, TV, Kids, and Shorts all failed simultaneously, generating 1.6 million reports on Downdetector. The root cause wasn't server failure or a hack — it was a bug in YouTube's recommendation algorithm, which drives 70% of all content watched on the platform. Without it, YouTube couldn't surface any content. Notably, ads continued to function throughout the outage.

top_posts.title: Complete n8n automation setup guide with AI workflows
top_posts.summary: n8n is a powerful open-source automation platform that allows users to create workflows connecting various services and APIs. The tutorial demonstrates setting up n8n both locally and in the cloud, creating automated news aggregation workflows that pull from RSS feeds, integrate AI summarization, and send notifications to Discord. Key features include visual workflow building, extensive service integrations, AI agent capabilities with tools and memory, and the ability to execute system commands for home lab automation.

top_posts.title: Free open-source remote desktop solution for all OS
top_posts.summary: A new open-source remote desktop solution supports Windows, Mac, and Linux and can be hosted personally, eliminating the need for costly RDP services. This solution addresses limitations of RDP, such as requiring Windows Pro and providing non-native performance for remote access across different networks. Alternatives like Guacamole, KasmVNC, and RustDesk offer diverse functionalities, with RustDesk being particularly praised for its features, performance, and hosting flexibility.

top_posts.title: Building AI agents with n8n using command line tools and ChatGPT
top_posts.summary: Demonstrates how to create AI agents in n8n that combine language models with command-line tools and memory. Shows a practical example of building an agent that can check website connectivity by executing ping commands through ChatGPT integration, highlighting the potential for automating network monitoring and system administration tasks.

top_posts.title: How I Set Up a Highly Technical Blogging Workflow with Obsidian, Hugo, Python, and GitHub
top_posts.summary: A reader is starting a blog inspired by Tiago Forte's book 'Building a Second Brain'. They're using a highly technical method involving Obsidian for note-taking, Hugo for converting markdown to HTML, GitHub for version control, and their chosen hosting provider. The goal is to make blogging seamless and integrated into their existing note-taking workflow. The post details the step-by-step setup process and emphasizes the importance of expressing and sharing ideas.

top_posts.title: Host AI Models Locally for Unlimited Access and Control
top_posts.summary: The post discusses the advantages of self-hosting AI models through Open Web UI, providing a cost-effective solution with unlimited access to various AI models. It details the process of setting up and running AI models on a virtual private server (VPS), allowing for extensive control over usage and data security. It also highlights the use of APIs and Light LLM to connect multiple AI services, offering a comprehensive guide to enhance AI interactions while managing costs effectively.
